criteria.limit_once: The row-limit parameter number appears in exactly one PARAM token, and the top-level LimitCount is that ParamRef. Any second use of the number rejects the descriptor, keeping the call-site LIMIT value out of filter positions.
criteria.limit_shared: The top-level LimitCount must be the row-limit ParamRef, but the same number may also appear in other PARAM tokens. Every site binds the single LIMIT value; the checker does not police reuse.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot decide limit exclusivity, or neither rule keeps the required contracts.

limit_exclusivity.instructions: Choose whether the row-limit parameter number may appear outside the LIMIT clause. Use common and topics.limit_exclusivity.

criteria.allow_trivia: Validity is exactly one RawStmt; leading and trailing semicolons, comments, and whitespace are preserved literally in the emitted segments. Copy-pasted statements keep working.
criteria.clean_ending: Validity is exactly one RawStmt plus no ASCII_59, SQL_COMMENT, or C_COMMENT token starting at or after the end of the last other token. Leading trivia is preserved; trailing semicolons and comments reject.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot decide trailing trivia, or neither rule keeps the required contracts.

trailing_semicolon.instructions: Choose whether trailing semicolons and comments are preserved or rejected. Use common and topics.trailing_semicolon.

fixed_constraints: P12 requires one statement per descriptor: a SELECT whose top-level LIMIT is the distinct row-limit parameter for one/optional/many, or INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE without RETURNING for execute. Application parameters are contiguous $1..$N matching the parameter record fields in order; the row-limit parameter is number N+1. The scanner splits static bytes into template segments; there is no second SQL lexer.

The manifest already enforces row_limit_parameter equal to len(parameters)+1 for row-returning descriptors and forbids it for execute. canlc checks each descriptor once per compile; checked descriptors are immutable data consumed by I35 query lowering, which binds the LIMIT from max_rows or 2.

Measured server behavior on PostgreSQL 17.11 through Bun 1.4.2 extended protocol: trailing semicolons, trailing whitespace, and trailing comments all execute; two statements reject with cannot insert multiple commands into a prepared statement; a LIMIT number reused as a filter value executes with one bound value at both sites.

Upstream span facts: RawStmt StmtLen is 0 unless the statement ends with a semicolon, so statement ends come from scanner tokens. Semicolons scan as ASCII_59; comments scan as SQL_COMMENT or C_COMMENT; SELECT 1 with any number of trailing semicolons yields exactly one RawStmt.
common.purpose: Advise the Can compiler strictly from the evidence supplied here. Do not browse, implement, or explain. When candidates cannot be separated on the evidence, choose the marked uncertainty outcome.

limit_exclusivity.facts: P12 calls the top-level LIMIT the distinct parameter after the application parameters. With parameters [term] and limit 2, a statement using $2 only in LIMIT binds the I35 call-site value once. A statement also filtering on $2 would silently route that same call-site value into the filter. Both shapes execute on the server; only the checker can distinguish intent from accident.

trailing_semicolon.facts: Authors copy SQL with trailing semicolons and comments from interactive clients. The server tolerates all trailing trivia and independently rejects genuine multi-statement input. Strictness here only affects which static bytes the compiler accepts, never runtime safety, since segments preserve bytes literally and values stay bound.
